newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU rejects BSE sheep tissue ban.
newsitem.headline: EU rejects BSE sheep tissue ban.

text.p: European Union farm ministers rejected by 10 votes to five a proposal to ban tissue from sheep and goats, as well as cattle, most likely to be affected with scrapie or mad cow disease, a French official said on Tuesday.

The European Commission, which has been accused of protecting farmers' incomes more than public health, said the measure was needed after British and French research showed that sheep could catch mad cow disease -- Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).
"The proposal was rejected," the French official said, adding that only France, Britain, Ireland, Sweden and Luxembourg voted in favour.
Under special EU voting rules, a simple majority of eight member states was required to throw out the proposal.

Other member states voted against, saying the measure was unnecessary and economically excessive given that their countries were virtually free of BSE and scrapie, a similar brain-wasting disease that has affected sheep for centuries.
Germany, supported by other member states, argued that the measure should be targeted on countries worst hit by the diseases.
Earlier this month, only Britain and France had supported the proposal when it was put to a vote by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee of senior national officials.
EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler refused to make concessions, arguing that no country was totally risk-free and national exemptions would distort trade in the 15-nation bloc.

The Commission's proposal, based on advice from EU veterinary scientists and the World Health Organistion, involved the removal of brains, eyes, spinal cord and spleen from sheep, cattle and goats over 12 months old and kept out of human and animal food.
